questions.question_text:
Which minimum set of labelled lengths is sufficient to find this rectangle's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\draw(0,0)--(5,0)node[midway,below]{$a$};\draw(5,0)--(5,3)node[midway,right]{$b$};\draw(5,3)--(0,3)node[midway,above]{$c$};\draw(0,3)--(0,0)node[midway,left]{$d$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: One length does not determine the rectangle's width.
These are equal opposite sides, so the width is still unknown.
Measuring all four sides repeats the two equal opposite lengths.

questions.solution_text: One side from each equal opposite pair is enough, so $a$ and $b$ are sufficient.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum number of side measurements needed for a square?

options.why: A second side repeats the same length because all square sides are equal.
Three measurements unnecessarily repeat the one equal side length.
Measuring every side ignores the square's equal-side property.

questions.solution_text: All four sides are equal, so one measurement is sufficient.

questions.question_text:
No equal sides are marked on this triangle. Which lengths are needed?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(1.5,3.5);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$p$};\draw(B)--(C)node[midway,above right]{$q$};\draw(C)--(A)node[midway,above left]{$r$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: The unmarked third side cannot be inferred from the other two.
One side gives no information about the other two sides.
The base length remains unknown and must also be measured.

questions.solution_text: Without equal-side information, every side is needed: $p$, $q$ and $r$.

questions.question_text: A regular pentagon has one side measured. How many more side measurements are needed?

options.why: A second measurement repeats the common side length.
The other sides are already known to equal the measured side.
This counts all sides again despite one already being measured.

questions.solution_text: Every side of a regular pentagon is equal, so no extra measurements are needed.

questions.question_text: A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides. What is the minimum number of side measurements needed?

options.why: One measurement gives only one of the two different side lengths.
A third measurement repeats a length from one equal pair.
Measuring all four sides ignores both equal-side pairs.

questions.solution_text: Measure one side from each equal pair, so $2$ measurements are needed.

questions.question_text: A rectangle has its top and bottom measured, but neither vertical side measured. What information is still needed?

options.why: Both horizontal sides are already known and are equal.
Only one is needed because opposite vertical sides are equal.
The rectangle's width is still unknown, so the perimeter cannot yet be found.

questions.solution_text: The two horizontal measurements repeat one length. One vertical side length is still required.
